ink-mark.canonical: color-mix(in srgb, #9cb8eb 45%, transparent) over the white PDF page (ink.3, not remapped)

body-text.canonical: #151a21 (gray.9, black, bright; tooltip ground in light)

body-text-dark.canonical: #e9ecf1 (gray.9 role, --mantine-color-text in dark; tooltip ground in dark)

display.purpose: The one empty-state heading that names the folder or the state.

headline.purpose: Each question at the top of its turn; dir=auto for Arabic.

title.purpose: Modal titles and headings inside an answer.

wordmark.purpose: "Atlas" beside the folded-map mark in the top bar, neutral bright ink, Latin in both languages, the only 700 weight.

body.purpose: Answer prose (max 75ch), suggested questions, composer text. Arabic interface text takes a 1.6 line height.

body-sm.purpose: Tree names, source rows, tables, trace, form labels, usage line.

label.purpose: Badges, source numbers, the Sources heading, sheet letters and row numbers; sentence case.

mono.purpose: SQL and tool input in the trace only.

shadows.name: xs / page
shadows.purpose: The rendered PDF page on the viewer stage.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Theme step; not used directly by app components.

shadows.name: md / overlay
shadows.purpose: Menus, popovers, comboboxes (model picker, voice picker).

shadows.name: lg / modal
shadows.purpose: Viewer and confirmation modals, over the overlay veil (32% ink in light, 62% near-black in dark).

shadows.name: xl
shadows.purpose: Theme step; not used directly by app components.

shadows.name: float-edge (dark)
shadows.purpose: A shadow does not read on the near-black page, so modals take a hairline edge in dark and sit on the raised surface.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Theme motion token: finished parts fade and rise (4px turns, 2px tree rows), folder open and close, collapses, AppShell and modal transitions, trace chevron.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Background, colour and border changes on rows, quiet controls and the composer focus border; the tree chevron turning; tooltips fade at 150ms.

motion.name: caret-pulse
motion.purpose: The streaming ink caret; static under reduced motion.

motion.name: avatar-loop
motion.value: requestAnimationFrame; pose eases with a 110ms half-life, the mouth with 45ms
motion.purpose: The call avatar only, while a call is open (The Living Face Rule). Paused in a hidden tab; a still pose per state under reduced motion.

motion.name: avatar-blink
motion.value: 180ms (70ms close, 110ms open), every 2.8 to 6.5s, sometimes a quick second blink
motion.purpose: Call avatar blinks while its eyes are open.

motion.name: avatar-breath
motion.value: 4.2s sine, 0.7 units of rise in a 120-unit drawing
motion.purpose: Call avatar breath for the whole open call.

motion.name: avatar-ring-turn
motion.purpose: The dashed ring while the call connects and while a spoken question runs; no animation under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: xs
breakpoints.purpose: Below it a source place always drops under its name; the call avatar drops to 56px with heavier lines, call controls grow to 40px, and only the latest caption shows.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Below it the sidebar folds behind a burger, the sheet goes edge to edge with only its top hairline, language and theme move to the sidebar foot, Clear chat becomes an icon, the cost pair moves to the composer hint line, and the viewer goes full screen.

narrative.overview:
Atlas is the category standard for chat-with-your-documents tools, built to the craft of Claude.ai's calm reading column (and its question box under the heading on a fresh chat), Perplexity's numbered sources and Linear's dense, quiet chrome with the content on an inset sheet. The owner chose the conventions on purpose and the build doesn't dress them up. The 52px top bar and the 300px sidebar are one continuous cool-neutral chrome field. The conversation sits on it as an inset sheet: the page ground, a 1px hairline and 8px corners, scrolling on its own while the chrome stays still. The sheet holds one 760px column. Everything is drawn with 1px hairlines on flat grounds. The one ink blue appears only where the reader acts or where the system points at evidence.

The same world runs in two schemes and two languages. Dark is the same roles on blue-black slate: the chrome darkest, the page a step up, raised surfaces a step above that. Every gray, ink, amber and red shade is a role, not a lightness step, and each role has its dark value, so a component that asks for "dimmed" or "red tint" reads correctly in both. Arabic mirrors the whole layout, while content (answers, questions, quotes, table cells, file names) keeps its own direction. Figures are Western digits in both languages, so a number on screen matches the number in the file.

Density follows Linear more than a marketing page. Tree rows are 13px names over 12px meta. Tables run at 13px with tabular figures. The answer reads at 15px with a 75ch measure. Motion only marks state changes: a hover tint, a chevron turning, a folder opening, and the finished answer's table and sources settling in once with a short fade-and-rise. One exception, approved by the owner on 2026-10-29: during a voice call, Atlas's face (a philosopher's bust in graphite line work, marble in both schemes) moves continuously, and nothing else does.

The system refuses the demo look named in the direction contract: decorative gradients, glowing AI sparkles, bubble chat and cards inside cards. The question is a heading-weight line, not a bubble. The answer is plain prose on the page ground, not a card.
keyCharacteristics: One brand hue (deep ink blue, shade 7 in light and shade 6 in dark of a 10-step ramp) for actions, focus, selection, links, citations, the open file, the streaming caret and the call avatar's ring while Atlas speaks
One chrome field (top bar and sidebar) with the conversation on an inset sheet of page ground
Light and dark schemes from one set of colour roles; the PDF page and the bust stay white in both
1px hairline borders instead of shadows on every resting surface; floating surfaces also take a hairline edge in dark
One system UI family for everything (Segoe UI carries Arabic on Windows); monospace only for SQL and tool input
Tabular Western figures wherever numbers appear, in English and Arabic
The whole layout mirrors in Arabic; content keeps its own direction
Continuous motion lives only in the call avatar, and only while a call is open

rules.name: The Ink Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Ink blue marks only what you can act on and where an answer points (primary action, focus, link, selection, active citation, cited text, the open file, streaming caret, and the call avatar's ring while Atlas speaks). The wordmark and its mark, headings, icons and the drawing of the bust stay neutral.

rules.name: The Colour Means Trouble Rule
rules.body: Amber and red mean a file or request has a problem, nothing else. Document types and the ok state use neutral badges, empty and skipped files use gray, and "not found" answers use a neutral notice.

rules.name: The Roles Not Shades Rule
rules.body: A component asks for a role (gray 6 for dimmed, red 1 for the error tint, `--atlas-surface` for a raised surface) and never for a lightness. The dark scheme gives every role its own value, so nothing is coloured per scheme in a component. The only fixed values are the ones that are real objects: the white PDF page and the marble bust.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every place a number appears sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Numeric table columns align right and never wrap.

rules.name: The Western Digits Rule
rules.body: Numbers are Western digits with comma thousands separators in both languages (counts, sizes, pages, amounts, times), the same as the documents and answers. Amounts are shown exactly as the data holds them, never rounded. Arabic counts use the noun's own plural form around the figure ("ملفان", "3 ملفات", "11 ملفًا").

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and badges are sentence case at zero tracking. The build has no uppercase or letterspaced text.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface that sits in the page gets a 1px border and no shadow. A shadow means the surface floats above the page, and in dark a floating surface also carries a hairline edge.

rules.name: The Fade Above The Dock Rule
rules.body: The one gradient in the system is functional: a 24px band above the docked composer that runs from transparent to the page ground, so turns scrolling under the composer fade out instead of being cut at its edge. It uses only the page ground, never a hue, and it is never decoration. No other surface takes a gradient.

rules.name: The Living Face Rule
rules.body: Continuous motion is allowed inside the call avatar only, and only while a call is open: blinks every 2.8 to 6.5s, a slow 4.2s breath, brows up while the user speaks, eyes up while a question runs, the mouth following Atlas's measured voice, and the ring dashed and turning while the call connects and while it checks. Under reduced motion it holds one still pose per state, and it does not move in a hidden tab. Every other surface keeps motion for state changes only.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius and shadow from the Mantine theme (`theme.ts`). Components carry no hex values.
Do ask for colour roles (gray 0 to 9, ink, yellow and red shades, `--atlas-surface`, `--atlas-focus`) so each surface reads in both schemes (The Roles Not Shades Rule).
Do keep ink blue to actions, focus, selection, links, citations, the open file, the streaming caret and the call avatar's speaking ring (The Ink Is Evidence Rule).
Do separate resting surfaces with 1px hairlines on chrome, page or surface grounds, and keep shadows for modals, menus and the PDF page; give floating surfaces a hairline edge in dark.
Do keep the conversation on the inset sheet, which scrolls on its own inside the still chrome field.
Do put the question box under the heading until the first question, then dock it at the sheet's foot with the page-ground fade above it.
Do set every figure in tabular Western digits and right-align numeric columns physically, in both languages.
Do use logical properties so the whole layout mirrors in Arabic, `dir="auto"` on content, and isolates around file names, paths and codes inside Arabic sentences.
Do keep SQL, formulas, paths and the Excel grid left to right in both languages.
Do join an amount and its currency, and a number and its unit, with a no-break space.
Do use 150ms ease-out for hover and colour changes and 180ms `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for content settling in, collapsing or a folder opening, and disable both under reduced motion.
Do use Tabler outline icons at 1.5 to 2 stroke, sized 12 to 18px.
Do give the call avatar a still pose per state under reduced motion, and stop its motion in a hidden tab (The Living Face Rule).
donts: Don't use decorative gradients, glowing AI sparkles, chat bubbles or cards inside cards. The page-ground fade above the docked composer is the only gradient (The Fade Above The Dock Rule).
Don't colour document types or ok files. Amber and red are for files and requests with problems only.
Don't put a shadow on a surface that sits in the page, including the inset sheet.
Don't pick a colour per scheme inside a component, or turn the PDF page or the bust dark.
Don't set uppercase or letterspaced labels. Labels are sentence case at 12px/600.
Don't add a second typeface or a display face. Monospace is for SQL and tool input only.
Don't use Eastern Arabic digits or round an amount for display.
Don't translate the wordmark, file names, item codes or numbers.
Don't choreograph page loads. Motion marks state changes only, except inside the call avatar while a call is open.
Don't colour the bust. Its drawing stays graphite on white marble in both schemes, and ink touches only its ring while Atlas speaks.
